lesson.child_mission: Converting between metres and centimetres uses 1 m = 100 cm. Multiply metres by 100 to get centimetres; group hundreds of centimetres into metres.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Convert: 5 m; 780 cm; 1 m 8 cm to centimetres only.

FEEDBACK
500 cm; 7 m 80 cm; 108 cm.

WATCH FOR
Treating 1 m as 10 cm (confusing with mm↔cm) breaks conversions.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Complete sixteen conversions both ways (m↔cm), including mixed metres-and-centimetres. Self-mark with the 100 rule written at the top.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.explain:
Converting between metres and centimetres uses 1 m = 100 cm. Multiply metres by 100 to get centimetres; group hundreds of centimetres into metres.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
